spec_match.rationale: All four caching forms from CSS Values 5 (default independent, --dashed-ident slot, per-element, fixed) are shown with their real declaration text and matching semantics, mirroring the suite's behavioural assertions.

interactive.rationale: Four aria-pressed mode buttons plus Regenerate rebuild twelve bars and a measured-from-render stats table (distinct heights/opacities, square count, range).

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index promises 'what each one does to the same layout' and the page delivers a per-mode visual plus measured distinctness.

edge_cases.rationale: The unsupported branch is clearly labelled simulation, but the simulation quietly idealises: per-element mode derives opacity deterministically from height and --paired always yields perfect squares, so a visitor on a pre-155 browser sees cleaner numbers than a real engine would ever produce, and no mode shows the common mistake the copy mentions (fixed-when-you-meant-per-element side by side).

references.rationale: Links https://chromestatus.com/feature/5324559251275776 and the random-caching spec section.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite asserts the two distinguishing behaviours (per-element distinctness, fixed collapsing to one value) rather than only parse checks — exactly the contracts this page teaches.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp) via CDP: fixed mode measured 1 distinct height of 12 (98px–98px), --paired mode 12/12 square bars with 11 distinct heights, Regenerate re-rolled; banner correctly labels everything as JS simulation on this browser; console clean, no exceptions; screenshots both viewports.

telemetry_health.rationale: Each build logs and emits showcaseTelemetry.assert('caching-mode-rendered', …) with mode, distinct counts and support flag.

design_system.rationale: Token colours, pressed mode buttons swap background and color together, 44px targets, stats measured not asserted.

accessibility.rationale: Mode buttons are real buttons with aria-pressed, the bar row is role=img with a text description of the rendered range, the stats table has caption and scopes, and the readout is aria-live.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: 0px horizontal overflow at 360x740 DPR3 and 1280x800 over CDP (the bar row scrolls internally by design); both screenshots clean.

openQuestions.title: Note that the pre-155 numbers are idealised simulation
openQuestions.detail: On a browser without random() the --paired mode always produces 12/12 squares and per-element derives opacity from height by a fixed linear map — cleaner than any real sample could be. The banner does say 'simulated', but the stats table presents these as 'Measured from the rendered bars', which is technically true yet gives spec-perfect numbers a real engine's independent draws would not (e.g. distinct-heights can collide). One sentence in the table caption or note distinguishing 'measured from the simulation' from 'measured from engine-resolved random()' would remove the ambiguity.

openQuestions.title: Add the wrong-tool comparison the copy promises
openQuestions.detail: The fixed-mode explainer calls fixed 'a common mistake when you meant per-element', but the page never shows the mistake as a mistake — e.g. a card-deal or avatar-tint mini-case rendered twice, once with fixed and once with per-element, so the reader sees identical-everything versus varied. Could live on this page as a second stage or as a new concept.

summary: The caching taxonomy is accurate and the measured-stats approach is the right instrument; verified over CDP on Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp) at http://localhost:3000/v155/css-random-function/caching-controls/ — mode switching, Regenerate, fixed collapsing to one height and --paired forcing squares all behaved, with an honest simulation banner since random() is unsupported here; console clean, no overflow either class. Feature /conformance/ route ran 0 pass / 8 fail, all honest pre-155 gaps. Open questions are refinements: label the simulation's idealised numbers, and show the fixed-vs-per-element mistake as a concrete before/after.
